original_question: When a multi-agent system is represented across several limiting descriptions, including microscopic dynamics, mean-field limits, graph limits, and embedding-based representations, how do optimal control problems behave under those limiting procedures? In particular, when passing between these scales, what properties of the control problem are preserved, changed, or lost?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, immediately after equation (42) and Figure 7: the future-direction prompt asking for a control-theoretic understanding of the mean-field, graph-limit, and embedding passages between multiscale descriptions of the same multi-agent system, explicitly 'in the spirit of Section 4.2.' ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's actual target as a multiscale control question, not a specific application model: it is about controlled multi-agent systems viewed through microscopic, mean-field, graph-limit, and embedding descriptions, and about what happens to the control problem when one passes between those scales. It also correctly places the emphasis on limiting procedures rather than on a single theorem already proved. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))
missing_details: The draft does not anchor the question to the specific heterogeneous microscopic system used in Section 5.1, namely dot ξ_i = (1/N) Σ_{j=1}^N G(t, x_i, x_j, ξ_i, ξ_j). ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It omits that x_i are fixed agent parameters, with dot x_i = 0, and that this heterogeneity is the point of the model: it lets G depend on the individual particle and bypasses the indistinguishability assumption of classical mean-field theory. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It does not say that the nearby discussion keeps the ambient state space for ξ_i and parameter space for x_i abstract; a faithful rewrite should therefore not invent extra Euclidean, manifold, or regularity assumptions that are not stated there. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It leaves out the full list of representations appearing in Figure 7: particle/microscopic, Liouville/probabilistic, Vlasov/mesoscopic mean-field, Euler/macroscopic graph-limit, together with embedding connections. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It does not specify what the paper means by graph-limit in this context: one passage is by viewing the right-hand side of (42) as a Riemann sum, and another nearby interpretation is via graphons and convergence in the cut norm. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It does not indicate that the intended scope is controlled by Section 4.2, which is the paper's concrete template for 'control across scales.' ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It omits the key obstruction from Section 4.2: under a naive mean-field passage, the limiting control ν may be singular with respect to μ and therefore have no effect on the limiting dynamics. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It does not mention the two concrete positive mechanisms already supplied by the paper as guidance: restricting to absolutely continuous controls ν = f μ with Radon-Nikodym derivative f, or splitting the population into m controlled leaders and N followers with N → ∞ and m fixed. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

It does not record the strongest paper-nearby control conclusion available in this direction, namely Γ-convergence of the leader-follower optimal control problems from the microscopic system (24)-(25) to the mixed ODE-PDE limit (26)-(27). ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

Its phrase 'what properties are preserved, changed, or lost' is slightly broader than the paper's wording. The closest paper-faithful sharpening is to ask for a meaningful limiting control theory and convergence behavior of the control problems under those multiscale limits. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))
refined_question: For controlled versions of the heterogeneous N-agent system dot ξ_i = (1/N) Σ_{j=1}^N G(t, x_i, x_j, ξ_i, ξ_j), where x_i are fixed agent parameters (dot x_i = 0) and ξ_i is the state of agent i, how do the associated optimal control problems behave under the multiscale limiting procedures discussed around Figure 7—namely the passages from the particle description to the Liouville, Vlasov (mean-field), Euler (graph-limit, including the Riemann-sum/graphon viewpoint), and embedding representations? More specifically, in the spirit of Section 4.2, can one formulate the controls so that these passages yield nontrivial limiting controlled dynamics and meaningful convergence of the optimal control problems, rather than a degenerate limit in which the limiting control becomes ineffective? ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5.1 rather than another part of the paper, because its keywords match the discussion following equation (42) and Figure 7: microscopic dynamics, mean-field limits, graph limits, and embeddings. But Section 5.1 states the problem only at a high level. Section 4.2 provides the hidden scope and intended meaning by showing both the pathology to avoid (singular limiting controls that lose effectiveness) and the model cases where one does get meaningful limits, including the leader-follower Γ-convergence result. The refined question therefore stays close to the paper's actual intent while making the underlying model, limit types, and control-theoretic stakes explicit. ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))
